littĕrĭo (lītĕr- ), ōnis, m. litterae,
I.a language-master, in a contemptuous sense: “appellare (aliquem) loquacem talpam, et purpuratam simiam, et litterionem Graecum,” Amm. 17, 11, 1 ; so, Graecus, Aug. adv. Leg. et Proph. 1, § 52.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
